t: Minimum Absolute Difference Between Elements With Constraint — Sliding Window Ordered Set
o: Find min |nums[i]−nums[j]| with |i−j| ≥ x. Sweep j from left to right; once j ≥ x, all indices ≤ j−x are eligible partners. Insert them into an ordered multiset as they become eligible, and for each new nums[j] binary-search its closest predecessor and successor. Example 1: when j=3, 4 is already in the set → difference 0.
k: Sliding window of eligible values in a balanced BST; nearest-neighbor query per step.

a.i: Maintain a sorted container of nums[0..j−x]; for each j query floor/ceiling of nums[j] and take the min gap.
s: For j from 0 to n−1: if j ≥ x, insert nums[j−x] into the sorted container.
Look up the largest value ≤ nums[j] and smallest ≥ nums[j]; update the answer.
a.t: O(n log n) — n inserts and searches in an ordered structure (array-splice versions degrade toward O(n²) worst case but pass typical tests)

a.i: For each pair with |i−j| ≥ x compute the difference directly — only viable for tiny n, useful as a correctness oracle.
s: Double loop over i<j with j−i ≥ x.

w: Lead with the ordered-set window; mention brute force only as a sanity check. Edge cases: x = 0 (every earlier element is eligible immediately) and early exit when ans hits 0.
